thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - NCCL communicator errors detected on prod-gpu-4 pool. 12 distinct worker containers logged 'NCCL WARN/ERR: comm 0x' and then stalled. Auto-retry hit 3 times.
incident-bot: Pager triggered (P1). Notifying on-call. Link: https://pager.redwood/incident/3067801234
emma_sre: I'm on it. Starting triage — which jobs are affected?
josh_oncall: looks like 3 active customer jobs (cust-a, cust-b, internal-train-46). All are tp4 tensor-parallel jobs.
maria_ml: cust-a is a 384B token inference batch, cust-b is a training mini-epoch checkpoint. internal-train-46 is low priority but currently running lots of small batches.
emma_sre: can someone paste the most recent container logs and dmesg/Xid traces?
raj_infra: pulling logs from prod-gpu-4 nodes:
raj_infra: ```
[2026-03-15T02:00:45Z] nv_peer_mem: device 0000:3b:00.0 error: Xid 79 0x7e2f0000
[2026-03-15T02:00:46Z] nccl: WARN ~ commId 0x7f94e3a0 - Allreduce stalled, lastSeen=5.2s
[2026-03-15T02:00:47Z] cuda: driver: GPU kernel panic - GPU 2 reset required
[2026-03-15T02:00:48Z] containerd: oom kill invoked for pid 4382 (python)
```
emma_sre: Xid 79 again, GPU reset. That's consistent with kernel/driver glitch leading to NCCL hang.
li_platform: network metrics show a brief spike in eth0 interrupts on node prod-gpu-4-7 at 02:00:44, coincident with the first warn. Could be NIC flaps affecting RDMA.
maria_ml: interesting — tp4 uses NVLink + IB; if RDMA flaps, rendezvous can fail and NCCL may go into blocked state.
josh_oncall: customer impact: cust-a latency > 10x, cust-b training stopped at checkpoint save, internal-train-46 retried and failed a few batches. I notified customer success for cust-a and cust-b.
emma_sre: immediate mitigations: 1) failover cust-a inference to hosted-fallback model (smaller replica) to reduce immediate customer impact; 2) drain suspect node and restart GPU driver; 3) if drain takes too long, restart affected containers with NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME override to prefer eth1.
li_platform: starting drain of prod-gpu-4-7, marking node unsched: `kubectl cordon prod-gpu-4-7 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data prod-gpu-4-7`
raj_infra: vendor driver patch available but requires maintenance window; quick action is driver restart: `systemctl restart nvidia-drivers` then `sudo nvidia-smi -r` on the node.
emma_sre: @maria_ml can you reroute cust-a? We have an app-level routing rule to prefer hosted variants.
maria_ml: rerouting now via console: applied route -> hosted-fallback/compressed-1g. Confirming traffic shift.
maria_ml: cust-a now 95% routed to hosted-fallback, latency dropped to 1.2s (was 8-12s). :thumbsup:
josh_oncall: cust-b training job is stuck in barrier, we should evict the pod to let the checkpoint resume on new workers. I'll do a graceful delete with `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30` on the affected pods.
emma_sre: do it, and note the job will re-schedule; checkpoint integrity might be OK but open a support ticket if state is corrupted.
raj_infra: driver restart completed on prod-gpu-4-7. Post-restart dmesg shows no Xid in the last 30s, nv_peer_mem reinitialized.
li_platform: after driver restart we saw NCCL recover logs: `nccl: INFO comm 0x7f94e3a0 resumed, peers reconnected`. Network counters normalized.
josh_oncall: pods restarted, cust-b resumed training and hit checkpoint save at 02:10:12. internal-train-46 continued with reduced throughput.
emma_sre: good. Now run a health sweep: run our collective-test harness against the pool for 5 loops.
maria_ml: running harness: `python -m tests.collective_smoke --pool prod-gpu-4 --iters 5`
maria_ml: loop1 OK, loop2 OK, loop3 spike at 5th second but recovered, loop4/5 OK. Looks stable.
emma_sre: risk assessment: probable cause = transient NIC interrupt/routing glitch causing RDMA packet loss leading to NCCL communicator stall and subsequent GPU reset (Xid 79). Impact: 3 jobs affected, small customer outage for cust-a (10 minutes degraded), cust-b training pause (~12 min), internal job recovered.
li_platform: mitigation summary posted to status page. We'll keep node cordoned for 30m observation before reprovisioning.
raj_infra: follow-up actions (short): 1) schedule driver upgrade + NIC firmware rollback validation in next maintenance window; 2) add NIC interrupt alerts to prod-gpu pool; 3) add NCCL healthkill fallback to force-terminate stuck communicators earlier (tunable).
emma_sre: assigning owners: raj -> driver/firmware, li -> alerting, maria -> routing/fallback playbooks, josh -> customer comms follow-through. I'll create incident ticket and link postmortem doc.
josh_oncall: CS notified, cust-a accepted routed fallback and we offered credit. cust-b engineering contact wants full postmortem. Sent note.
incident-bot: Incident 3067801234 created: https://incidents.redwood/3067801234; severity=P1; status=mitigated -> monitoring.
emma_sre: moving to handoff: @oncall-next (emma_sre) — if anything recurs ping pager. Closing active triage, will run 1h stabilization check and then convert to postmortem ticket.
maria_ml: quick note for postmortem: attach the harness logs, nv_peer_mem traces, dmesg, and routing change history. Also add suggested runbook update: on NCCL stalls, try routing to hosted fallback before node drain when customer-critical.
li_platform: leaving node cordoned until 03:00Z for observation.
emma_sre: thanks everyone. Good coordination. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Reaction summary: :thumbsup: x4, :rotating_light: x1
